# Outbound endpoint

One outbound endpoint of a DNS private resolver (`Microsoft.Network/dnsResolvers/outboundEndpoints`):
where queries that match a forwarding ruleset's rules leave the resolver's virtual network for their
target DNS servers. The root module calls it once per endpoint; it can also be called alone with the
resolver's resource ID.

Azure cannot move an endpoint to another subnet, so changing `subnet_id` replaces it. Azure deletes an
outbound endpoint only once no ruleset uses it: take it out of the rulesets in one apply and delete it in
the next. For the same reason a new `subnet_id` fails while a ruleset uses the endpoint (the replacement
keeps its name and ID, and deletes it first): create an endpoint with another name in the new subnet,
point the rulesets at it, then remove this one.

## Required Inputs

The following input variables are required:

### <a name="input_location"></a> [location](#input\_location)

Description: Azure region of the outbound endpoint: the resolver's.

Type: `string`

### <a name="input_name"></a> [name](#input\_name)

Description: Name of the outbound endpoint. Changing it replaces the endpoint.

Type: `string`

### <a name="input_parent_id"></a> [parent\_id](#input\_parent\_id)

Description: Resource ID of the DNS private resolver that holds the endpoint.

Type: `string`

### <a name="input_subnet_id"></a> [subnet\_id](#input\_subnet\_id)

Description: Resource ID of the endpoint's subnet: in the resolver's virtual network, /28 to /24, delegated to `Microsoft.Network/dnsResolvers`, and used by no other endpoint or service. Changing it replaces the endpoint, which Azure refuses while a ruleset uses it: create another endpoint, point the rulesets at it, then remove this one.

Type: `string`

## Outputs

The following outputs are exported:

### <a name="output_lock_dependency"></a> [lock\_dependency](#output\_lock\_dependency)

Description: Changes whenever the endpoint is created, replaced or changed. The caller passes it in the resolver's `lock_dependencies`: Azure applies the resolver's lock to the endpoint too, and a `ReadOnly` lock also blocks updating it in place, which keeps its ID.

### <a name="output_name"></a> [name](#output\_name)

Description: Name of the outbound endpoint.

### <a name="output_resource_id"></a> [resource\_id](#output\_resource\_id)

Description: Resource ID of the outbound endpoint.
